sentences.span: a big chunk of Monday's rally was dealers being forced to buy. And as of this morning, with the vol meltdown stalled, so is the rally.
sentences.why: McElligott's note frames the rally as mechanical dealer hedging, not organic demand; this is his bank's stance, stated in the source.

sentences.span: Dealers who sold all those puts hedged by shorting futures... Dealers had to buy back a BRICK of Short $Delta / Futures
sentences.why: Matches the mechanism exactly: short puts hedged with short futures, unwound as vol/delta collapsed, forcing futures buybacks.

sentences.span: the Nomura cross-asset guru says the breadth was the sideshow... the far and away standout story... was the absolutely epic Vol Crush
sentences.why: Direct paraphrase of McElligott's own framing of breadth as sideshow and the vol collapse as the real story.

sentences.span: the same strategist now writes that "the capitulation process is far along"... and keeps his S&P 500 target at 8,000
sentences.why: Lakos-Bujas's capitulation call and unchanged 8,000 target match; target's year-end framing is consistent with the companion JPM note's forward-looking (2027) context and not contradicted anywhere.

sentences.span: a marginal new low, on less selling pressure than last Thursday, somewhere between 7,100 and 7,300... a classic re-test
sentences.why: Exact match for Wilson's stated 7,100-7,300 retest range and rationale.

sentences.span: the past two weeks were the most active ever for AI CDS, with $8-10 billion trading every week, roughly seven times the run-rate of a year ago
sentences.why: Verbatim figures for weekly AI CDS turnover and the multiple versus a year ago.

sentences.span: on a day when the NDX fell 6.4% and the S&P 4.4%, CDX IG widened just 3.5bps
sentences.why: Figures match exactly; attribution to Goldman's credit desk (McCarthy/Pasi) is correct, and 'Nasdaq' is standard shorthand for the Nasdaq-100 figure quoted.

sentences.span: for AI deals specifically, November's monthly average is north of 18bps
sentences.why: Directly supports 'ran above 18 basis points in November.'

sentences.span: at $1.7 trillion in 2027, against a $1.3 trillion consensus... no less than about $1.5 trillion... $1.5 trillion next year adds 4-5% to 2027 index earnings
sentences.why: All four figures (capex, consensus, floor, EPS sensitivity, earnings impact) match exactly.

sentences.span: banks shelved the junk bond sale for Anthropic's $15 billion Texas data center (Oct 29)
sentences.why: Exact match for company, amount, location, and date.

sentences.span: tracking the path of our silver stock analog... they also say the first bounce gets sold
sentences.why: Matches Wilson's silver-miner analog for semis and its implication that the first rally should be sold.

sentences.span: AI themes...still makes up ~32% of total US net exposure...reduction from peaks back in June (47%) with HFs now tracking ~2% underweight
sentences.why: All three figures (32%, 47% June peak, ~2% underweight) match exactly.

sentences.span: assuming 60 tonnes a month of official buying through 2026-27, compared with a seasonally adjusted three-month average of 85 tonnes a month... drives most of the 15% price upside we forecast by end-2027
sentences.why: All figures (60 tonnes assumed, 85 tonnes current pace, 15% upside, end-2027) match exactly.

sentences.span: the cheapest marginal supplier with spare power is China... China builds power ten times faster
sentences.why: TS Lombard's own argument ties cheap/abundant Chinese power directly to China's (Huawei's) ability to keep closing the compute-share gap on Nvidia.

sentences.span: This is part of the China Tech Shock... Risk falls on the margins of the western hardware names... Shrinking profits for Western tech
sentences.why: Matches TS Lombard's thesis that China becomes the low-cost compute supplier and the risk to Western tech is margin compression, not weaker demand.
